candidates.summary: The Federal Reserve released minutes from its September 15-16 meeting showing that most participants believed another increase in the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year-end. The minutes said future decisions would remain dependent on incoming information, the economic outlook and the balance of risks.
candidates.title: Federal Reserve minutes point to another 2026 rate increase

candidates.summary: Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine killed at least 28 people and injured about 100, according to a late update from Ukraine's interior minister. The largest reported loss was in Pryluky, where a missile destroyed a residential building. Ukrainian officials said energy and industrial facilities were also damaged; Russia said it targeted military-industrial sites.
candidates.title: Russian missile and drone barrage kills at least 28 in Ukraine

sources.name: Office of the President of Ukraine

candidates.summary: Saudi aviation authorities said attacks on Abha International Airport and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed three foreign residents and injured 36 people. The Abha attack occurred October 6, while the Riyadh attack killed a Sudanese resident on October 7. Saudi authorities did not attribute responsibility, but Yemen's Houthi movement claimed the airport attacks.
candidates.title: Attacks on Saudi airports kill three people

candidates.summary: CrowdStrike reported finding infrastructure and files associated with data theft from South Korean financial organizations in a campaign active from late September into early October. The company said the unidentified, likely Chinese-speaking and financially motivated actor used the open-source ARTEX agentic penetration-testing tool alongside large language models. CrowdStrike assessed the attribution indicators with moderate confidence and did not identify a named adversary.
candidates.title: CrowdStrike reports AI-assisted campaign against South Korean finance sector

candidates.summary: Russia's health regulator said it was winding down precautions following the death of an Irkutsk anti-plague institute worker from pneumonia of undetermined origin. It said tests had detected no dangerous pathogens among contacts and about 90% of roughly 200 people initially quarantined had been released. The World Health Organization requested further information about the cause, the pathogen that prompted precautions and reports of another employee with pneumonia.
candidates.title: Russia eases precautions after laboratory worker's unexplained death
